While I agree the price is high and they have also made a huge change in how they design and market blocks these days (ugh!), I wanted to mention one thing.

One reason for the high price is that LEGO has extremely high tolerances. They throw away molds way early in their production cycle in order to keep the high part tolerance. The tolerance is so good that people looking for a consistent stable build platform sometimes use legos as a basis- see the low priced AFM kit for teaching. They built a low-cost atomic force microscope using some lego parts due to how well they're made. (The scanner etc was obviously not lego, but the base etc, was.)

Producing plastic parts with that type of reproducibility definitely costs more than the average junk plastic we tend to associate with kids toys these days. (Ugh, Matchbox, I'm looking at you- your non-car toys are horrible.)
